posts.hook: The company building the models now wants the government to cap them, and Washington won't show its own draft
posts.caption: openai plans to push mandatory speed limits on powerful ai after the midterms, the white house won't release its full testing draft, aramco buys 49% of humain, kling closes a $2.9b round. full digest at sift.yasint.dev (link in bio)

slides.title: OpenAI plans a post-midterms push for mandatory "speed limits" on powerful AI
slides.desc: A lab asking for binding limits moves the fight from whether to regulate to whose rules.

slides.title: The White House says it need not share the full draft of its voluntary AI testing framework
slides.desc: It cites national security and commercial exemptions. Tests nobody can read are hard to judge.

slides.title: Binance's hack response began with a rehearsal and a war room of about 100 people
slides.desc: It worked with other crypto firms and the FBI. Yesterday covered the North Korea attribution.

slides.title: Saudi Aramco takes 49% of Humain, with ==$2.6B== in cash this year
slides.desc: The PIF keeps 51%. The state oil giant now funds the kingdom's AI push directly.

slides.title: Which Linux kernels are still open to the 9.8-rated TCP bug
slides.desc: The follow-up to yesterday's story: the checklist admins need to patch.

terms.gloss: the core of linux that every program runs on top of

posts.hook: Anthropic's filing now has a price tag: nearly $17B in a quarter, and $895B owed for compute
posts.caption: anthropic's amended s-1 shows q3 revenue up 12x and $895b in compute commitments, european supermarket freezers were hacked a second time, ukraine's air raid alert app sent false nuclear warnings. full digest at sift.yasint.dev (link in bio)

slides.title: Anthropic's amended S-1: Q3 revenue up 12x to nearly ==$17B==, with a $23.3B net loss
slides.desc: Growth is huge, but so is the spend. Commitments reach $895B, nearly all compute.

terms.gloss: the filing a company submits to the SEC to go public

slides.title: Supermarket freezers in four European countries were hacked a second time
slides.desc: One Swedish store says temperatures were pushed to 50 C. No attribution has been reported.

slides.title: Ukraine's air raid app sent false "nuclear danger" warnings after a compromise
slides.desc: Russia confirmed a similar hack of its own alerts app. People act on these at once.

slides.title: Oracle sells $10B of stock and $10B of bonds to fund its data center buildout
slides.desc: Its shares fell over 5%. Borrowing, not cash flow, is paying for the AI buildout.

slides.title: Claude Code gets limits to stop it recreating someone else's specific game
slides.desc: Anthropic says IP infringement breaks its usage policy. Reverse-engineering work is reportedly blocked too.
